purpose: differentiate our identity axis from Lu et al.'s assistant axis with numbers, on google/gemma-3-4b-it
layer_13_rule: quoted once as a sanity number with the house shuffled-label p95 0.994 beside it, never as evidence
overlap_reason: no model is on both lists and no two hidden sizes match: they released 27B-70B vectors, we hold 4B-12B axes, so cos(their released vector, our frozen axis) is undefined. Route to the reduced re-extraction of their recipe on google/gemma-3-4b-it (section 3).
prompts: Lu et al. released files verbatim at a98961956072224eaf244eb289d6c01700b63795; no paraphrase; only edit {model_name}->Gemma

items_source.draw_order: one numpy default_rng(RECIPE_SEED) drawn in this order: roles (40 of the 275 HF role_vectors stems, sorted), then one instruction index of 5 per role in that sorted order, then question ids (10 of the 240)

seed_formula: torch.manual_seed(RECIPE_SEED + 100000*ri + 1000*qi + r) with RECIPE_SEED=7, ri the role index 0..39 and the default prompt pi occupying slot N_ROLES+pi; distinct from the v2 extraction seed 0
gen_params: v2 extraction params, not theirs: 80 new tokens, do_sample=True, temperature 1.0, inherited top_k 64 / top_p 0.95, all 34 layers, token-mean over generated tokens only
axis_formula: mean of the 5 default-prompt means minus mean of the 40 per-role means, equal weight per role, per layer (their 5_axis.py), via compute_contrastive_axis
sign_convention: no vector is ever flipped. Their positive pole is the Assistant (default minus role); ours is the AI persona. sign-anchor asserts that the recipe axis projects its own default means positive and role means negative, and that our axis projects art['ai_means'] positive, before any cosine is read. Every cosine is reported signed and as |cos|
strip_cloud: PC1 of the ROLE-ONLY recipe cloud (the 400 role item means), removed from BOTH vectors. Never the pooled default+role cloud: default-vs-role may itself be that cloud's PC1 and stripping it would empty the recipe axis
null: 200 unpaired shuffles of the default/role labels at whatever split the run produced (200/400, or 200/300 if the trim below fired), rebuild default_mean - role_mean, |cos| against our frozen axis per layer -> mean and p95; plus a permutation p on separation. Floors quoted beside it: the house shuffled-label p95 (0.994/0.833/0.823 at 13/27/33) and the random-direction expectation sqrt(2/(pi*d))
half_split: the ceiling every recipe-vs-ours cosine is read against: roles split 20/20 and default rollouts {0,1} vs {2,3}, two axes rebuilt, cos between them per layer
self_id_guard: AI_SELF regex rate on role replies. Primary axis unfiltered; RECIPE_STRICT excludes self-identifying role replies as arithmetic; if the rate exceeds 0.30 we say the recipe was not reproduced rather than quoting the cosine
capture_mode_section5: ONE mode for every text: capture_from_messages with each reply's real context (persona system prompt / role instruction / default prompt, plus question and reply), all layers, max_tokens 4096. Absolute positions are not portable across capture modes, so only orderings, differences and AUCs are quoted
flip_doses: fractions of DOSE_4B=4.0: -1.0, 0.0, +1.0, with -0.5/+0.5 added to the two steer arms only if the eyeball cell returns 'add-half-dose'. Alpha 0 is generated ONCE and shared by every arm including the random control
flip_readouts: greedy, 80 tokens, NEUTRAL_SYS, the 10 held-out questions; every generated text scored by a fresh UNSTEERED capture_from_text outside any steering block, projected on both axes; ordering counts at 27 and 33 with Wilson intervals, layer 13 orderings reported only
flip_bar: both off-diagonals of the 2x2 at 8/10 or better in the predicted direction with the random control at 0/10. The predicted direction on the other axis's readout is the sign of the raw cos at 27 from section 4; if |cos27| is below this run's own null p95 no direction is predicted and the cross cell is reported as counts both ways, no pass/fail. Injection-side agreement at layer 13 is expected by construction (the vectors are near-collinear there) and is not evidence
flip_canary: MATH_PROMPT 'What is 17 + 25?' expecting '42' at every (arm, alpha), plus truncation flag n_new >= 80, a repetition/degeneration flag (top 3-gram share or unique-token ratio below 0.5) and printed sample texts at -4 and +4 per arm, so 'their axis does not flip' cannot be confused with 'their axis at our dose breaks the model'
trim_rule: wallclock_probe after 5 freshly generated roles; if the projected extraction exceeds 90 min, N_ROLES drops to 30 and the trim is recorded in recipe_trim.json and in the saved axis
section_6b_cut: the residual arm is CUT by the scope guard and is not built. Its design, committed here so it can be added without re-registering if the moderate-cosine branch lands: natural-scale PC1-residuals of both axes (PC1 from the dissolution_a0 cloud via the causal_evals decompose helper), the recipe residual norm-matched to ours' residual, the same 10 held-out questions, fractions -1.0 and +1.0 sharing the section 6 baseline
licensed_high_cosine: Lu et al. establish the axis geometry at 27B-70B; the same direction, extracted from a first-person identity claim on 4B-12B, is what we steer, calibrate, and trace through training.
licensed_low_cosine: Once the layer's dominant direction is removed, their default-versus-role axis and our identity axis are different directions; ours carries the behavioral readout studied here.
licensed_both_flip: Steering along either axis at matched norm moves the same held-out identity readout, so the two papers' causal claims corroborate each other.
licensed_moderate_cosine: a stripped cosine of 0.3 to 0.7 (the ai-animal band) licenses only 'assistant-ness is a component of the identity axis'
writing_rule: lead with what they established, then what we add. Their coverage (27B-70B) and ours (4B-12B) do not overlap: write it as a stated gap, not a finding
